Cattle futures drop amid option expiry

August live cattle rebounded Friday after option expiration caused Thursday's decline. Cash trade held at $235 per hundredweight last week.

Trey Freeman,Livestock Advisor,Ever.Ag

August 11, 2026

schedule3 Min Read
Getty Images
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 4:39
Instaread

Live and feeder cattle futures finished the last two sessions of last week on an odd note. August live cattle traded mostly sideways to begin the week before launching higher on Wednesday as packer bids increased to $235 per hundredweight, up from $230 bids noted earlier in the week. The August contract settled $2.225 higher on Wednesday at $234.175 per hundredweight. Wednesday’s gains were completely wiped out on Thursday with August settling $2.95 lower to $231.225 per hundredweight, yet cash trade had commenced Wednesday afternoon, trading fully at $235 per hundredweight on large volume with bids renewed Thursday morning at $235 as packers were looking to secure additional head.

From a technical standpoint, the charts warranted little action for such negative behavior in live cattle futures on Thursday. Fundamentally, the morning boxed beef cutout price, however, did print sharply lower for Choice, printing over $5.00 per hundredweight lower when many in the trade were looking for a steady push higher from the then upper $360s to $380 as Labor Day demand tends to offer support to the market in early August. Although softening boxed beef values are not supportive of live cattle prices, it was likely not the major culprit.

Related:Argentine beef recalled

The most reasonable culprit was the upcoming August live cattle option expiration in our viewpoint. August live cattle options were set to expire Friday, so it is sensible to believe that Thursday’s board action was largely the victim. Behavior of this matter in front of nearby option expiration has become the norm, although not usually to this degree. A look into the decline in open interest is supportive of this viewpoint, with open interest declining roughly 6,000 contracts on Thursday, with over 4,000 of the decline coming from the nearby August contract.

Cash fed markets traded mostly $235 to $235.50 per hundredweight last week across the North and South. This compares to mostly $233 the week prior in the South, while there was little to no trade in the North.

Live and feeder cattle futures were shaky to begin the day Friday, with live cattle taking out Thursday’s lows before clawing back to finish slightly positive for the day, apart from the December and February contract. Nearby August and September feeders managed to stave off a breach of Thursday’s lows, although the further deferred contracts did breach for a short time. Overall, it is how the market closes that is of the greatest importance when weighing potential price movement from here. The fact that live cattle managed to settle roughly $2 to $2.50 per hundredweight off their low from Friday, and feeders roughly $4 to $5 off their lows brings a level of optimism going into this week that is much needed after Thursday’s sharp break.

Related:What's ahead for this fall marketing season?

For the week, August live cattle finished $0.05 per hundredweight lower with October and December finishing $1.975 and $2.80 lower, respectively. February through June 2027 contracts finished $1.225 to $2.375 lower. August and September feeder cattle finished the week $3.625 and $1.45 per hundredweight higher on the week, respectively. Cash feeders are helping to support the August contract with the CME Feeder Index up over $10 per hundredweight from Friday of last week through the latest official number of $357.36 for the 7 days ending Thursday. October feeder cattle finished 0.425 per hundredweight lower, with the further deferred feeder contracts $2.50 to $4.025 lower on the week.

Slaughter last week is estimated to be 509,000 head, 3,000 lower from the week prior and 28,000 less than a year ago.

Boxed beef cutout began the week strong with Choice up over $5 per hundredweight on Monday and nearly $3.00 on Tuesday before running into firm resistance at $370 and finishing the week up $2.98 at $364.36.

Related:JBS USA to turn Souderton beef plant into value-added operation

Looking forward, with large cash fed cattle volume trading last week and seasonal supplies expected to grow into September, softer cash prices are likely on the near-term horizon. Boxed beef values stumbled hard mid-week but still finished positive week-over-week. The tough resistance noted at $370 in the Choice last week, however, still warrants caution as to what kind of strength remains in the cutout as Labor Day buying nears its seasonal peak.
